*   **Polynomial Degree Limit:** The predictor cannot recover the value of an $n$-th degree polynomial at the corner $v$ from the other corners because it cannot differentiate the monomial $x_1 x_2 \dots x_n$ (which is 1 at $v$ and 0 elsewhere on the cube) from the zero polynomial [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the predictor cannot recover the value of an n-th degree polynomial at corner v from other corners because it cannot differentiate the monomial x_1 x_2 ... x_n from the zero polynomial. Source [S1] explicitly states in the section '4. Prediction for polynomials': 'As a justification, consider the monomial x_1 x_2 ... x_n (the product of all coordinates). The product is zero on all vertices of the unit cube except for one. So, a predictor would not be able to differentiate this monomial from the zero polynomial. Hence, the values of the scalar field at the 2^n-1 corners of an n-dimensional cube are not sufficient to recover the value of an n th degree polynomial at the 2^n th corner.' This matches the claim exactly.
